name: winapp
description: WinApp extension for Visual Studio Code to assist in building, debugging, and packaging Windows applications. Includes a WinUI XAML language service and schema-aware IntelliSense for AppxManifest.xml files.

winapp.appDirectories.description: Relative paths (from the workspace root) to app project directories. When set, WinApp commands target these directories instead of auto-scanning. If multiple entries are provided, you'll be prompted to choose.

winapp.manifest.intelliSense.enable.description: Enable IntelliSense (completion, hover, diagnostics, and Go to Definition/navigation) for AppxManifest.xml files.

winapp.manifest.diagnostics.level.description: Diagnostic filter for manifest schema validation. Set to 'off' to disable validation, 'warning' to show all diagnostics, or 'error' to show only errors.

winapp.manifest.intelliSense.diagnostics.description: When enabled, report known manifest elements that appear under an unexpected parent even when substitution-group coverage is incomplete.

winapp.xaml.intelliSense.enable.description: Enable the WinUI XAML language server, including completion, hover, diagnostics, navigation, formatting, and other project-aware editor features.

enumDescriptions: Disable XAML diagnostics while keeping other IntelliSense features enabled.
winapp.xaml.diagnostics.level.description: Diagnostic filter for WinUI XAML validation.

enumDescriptions: Use the C# extension's XAML formatter when its XAML tools are enabled; otherwise use WinApp XAML IntelliSense.
Always use the WinApp XAML IntelliSense formatter.
Do not register the WinApp XAML formatter.
winapp.xaml.formatting.provider.description: Controls formatter coexistence with the C# extension's XAML tooling. Restart the XAML language server after changing this setting.

input.description: What to run: a project file (.csproj), a solution (.sln/.slnx), a directory containing one, or a build output folder containing your app binaries (e.g., '${workspaceFolder}/bin/Debug/net8.0-windows10.0.22621'). If not set, you will be prompted to select a target.

inputFolder.description: Path to the build output folder containing your app binaries. If not set, you will be prompted to select a folder.
inputFolder.deprecationMessage: Use "input" instead, which also accepts a project or solution file. If both are set, "input" wins.

project.description: Project mode only. The project to launch when "input" is a solution, or a directory holding more than one runnable app project. Accepts a project name or path. Ignored in folder mode. Defaults to the only runnable project, when there is exactly one.

configuration.description: Project mode only. The build configuration to use. Ignored in folder mode.

arch.description: Project mode only. Target architecture to build for. Ignored in folder mode, and ignored when "runtime" is set. Defaults to the current process architecture.

framework.description: Project mode only. Target framework moniker to build, for multi-targeted projects (e.g., 'net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0'). Ignored in folder mode. Defaults to the project's own target framework, which is unambiguous unless the project multi-targets.

runtime.description: Project mode only. Runtime identifier to build for (e.g., 'win-x64'). Overrides "arch". Only Windows RIDs are supported. Ignored in folder mode. Defaults to the RID for "arch", or for the current process architecture when neither is set.

properties.description: Project mode only. MSBuild properties to pass to the build, as name/value pairs. Ignored in folder mode. Defaults to none.

noBuild.description: Project mode only. Run the existing build output without rebuilding. Ignored in folder mode, which never builds.

noRestore.description: Project mode only. Do not restore the project before building. Ignored in folder mode, and has no effect when "noBuild" is set.

aot.description: Project mode only. Run the project's configured .NET Native AOT publish instead of an ordinary build. Requires an effective PublishAot=true and uses the native cppvsdbg debugger; an explicitly configured debuggerType must be cppvsdbg. Ignored in folder mode.

clean.description: Both modes. Remove the existing package's application data (LocalState and settings) before deploying. Application data is otherwise preserved across re-deployments.

unregisterOnExit.description: Both modes. Remove the development package registration after the application exits. Only removes packages registered in development mode.

withAlias.description: Both modes. Launch through the app's execution alias so stdin/stdout are inherited, instead of through AUMID activation. Console apps (OutputType=Exe) already launch this way, so this is for forcing it for a windowed app. The CLI adds the uap5:ExecutionAlias to the manifest it stages, so no manifest edit is needed. Cannot be combined with "withoutAlias".

withoutAlias.description: Both modes. Launch through AUMID activation even for a console app, which would otherwise use its execution alias. The app then runs without a console and prints nothing to the terminal. Cannot be combined with "withAlias".

executable.description: Folder mode only. Which executable to launch, relative to the input folder, when the manifest uses a $targetnametoken$ placeholder and the folder holds more than one .exe. Defaults to auto-detection.

manifest.description: Both modes. Path to the Package.appxmanifest file. Defaults to auto-detection from the input folder or the current directory; the CLI locates an existing manifest and never generates one.

debuggerType.description: Optional override for the underlying debugger to use. Omit to let WinApp reuse an installed debugger or prompt you to pick one ('coreclr', 'cppvsdbg', or 'node').

workingDirectory.description: Both modes. Working directory for the launched application. Defaults to the workspace folder.

args.description: Both modes. Command-line arguments to pass to the application. Defaults to none.

outputAppxDirectory.description: Both modes. Output directory for the loose layout package. Defaults to a directory named AppX inside the input directory.

configurationSnippets.label: WinApp: Launch and Attach
configurationSnippets.description: Launch a WinApp package and attach the debugger

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run sync-schemas && npm run verify-schemas && npm run package && node scripts/ensure-server-bundle.mjs
scripts.build: npm run compile-tsc && npm run compile && npm run build:server:debug
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tsc && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm run build:server:debug && npm run restore:fixture
scripts.test:e2e: npm run compile && npx playwright test --config=playwright.config.ts
scripts.test:server: npm run restore:fixture && dotnet test server/test/WinUiXaml.Xaml.Tests/WinUiXaml.Xaml.Tests.csproj -c Debug --nologo && dotnet test server/test/WinUiXaml.Workspace.Tests/WinUiXaml.Workspace.Tests.csproj -c Debug --nologo && dotnet test server/test/WinUiXaml.LanguageServer.Tests/WinUiXaml.LanguageServer.Tests.csproj -c Debug --nologo
scripts.test:xaml-smoke: npm run build:server:debug && npm run restore:fixture && node server/test/lsp-smoke/smoke.mjs
scripts.clean: node -e "require('fs').rmSync('bin', {recursive: true, force: true}); require('fs').rmSync('out', {recursive: true, force: true}); require('fs').rmSync('dist', {recursive: true, force: true});"
scripts.verify-schemas: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),p=require('path'),d=p.join(__dirname,'schemas');if(!fs.existsSync(d)||fs.readdirSync(d).filter(f=>f.endsWith('.xsd')).length===0){console.error('ERROR: schemas/ contains no XSD files. Run npm run sync-schemas first.');process.exit(1);}console.log('schemas/ verified:',fs.readdirSync(d).filter(f=>f.endsWith('.xsd')).length,'XSD files');"
